candidates.title: Premier says Manitoba nearing limits of what it can do on affordability, so he's going after big corporations
candidates.description: Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew says the provincial government is reaching the limits of what it can do to ease the cost of living without sacrificing the revenue needed to fund public services, and that corporate giants need to do their part.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Snowbirds set to fly iconic jets for last time this weekend
candidates.description: Fifty-five years after the team's formation, the Canadian Forces Snowbirds' iconic jets will grace the skies one last time. The aerobatics team's CT-114 Tutor jets are set to fly over Calgary's McMahon Stadium on Sunday as part of the 113th Grey Cup festivities, before being grounded permanently.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Change to Ontario's 'safer-supply' opioid prescriptions abruptly paused due to legal challenge
candidates.description: A controversial change to "safer-supply" opioid prescriptions in Ontario that would force recipients to take them in front of a pharmacist, rather than on their own schedule at home, has been abruptly paused due to a legal challenge. Critics said the proposal would drastically affect the lives of drug users while causing potential chaos at pharmacies.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 3 kids, 2 adults in life-threatening condition after Burlington, Ont., house fire: police
candidates.description: Five people, including three children, are in life-threatening condition in hospital after a house fire in Burlington on Saturday morning, Halton police say.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Margaret Atwood joins other bird lovers to fight against a proposed 600-foot tower on Pelee Island
candidates.description: Atwood called the location, which is one road over from the new Atwood-Gibson Bird Centre, "one of the stupidest places on the planet" to put a tower.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: These farmers are worried N.L. is facing another hay shortage
candidates.description: Farmers and livestock owners are once again at risk of running out of hay following a disastrous shortage last year, according to some farmers. Demand for hay is growing each year and production can’t keep up, says the owners of 3C Farms in Comfort Cove-Newstead.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Scam targeting minor hockey teams 'heartbreaking' for affected kids
candidates.description: Valerie Favreau, the chair of the Oromocto Minor Hockey Association, said two under-13 teams signed up for a tournament in Stanley, with each team losing around $750 in fake registration fees. It's a type of scam that is referred to as "spear phishing," according to the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Quebec assumes parents help pay for post-secondary schooling. Students say many can't
candidates.description: Thousands of post-secondary and university students held strikes across Quebec this week to denounce “austerity measures and growing precariousness” among students in the face of the rising cost of living and the provincewide housing crisis. Among other things, the coalition is calling for a reform of Quebec's student financial aid program.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Montreal's deteriorating Dieppe Park to get $35M makeover — but not any time soon
candidates.description: Montreal is planning a $35-million makeover for Dieppe Park, including replacing its crumbling riverfront retaining wall. But surfers, fishermen and visitors will have to wait until 2029 for work to begin, and even that tentative date depends on further planning and environmental approvals.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Crypto King' Aiden Pleterski testifies he was beaten, tortured during alleged kidnapping
candidates.description: Self-described "Crypto King" Aiden Pleterski described being beaten with a gun and tortured with knives and a lighter in the back of a truck as he began his testimony at the trial of his alleged kidnappers Friday in Toronto.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Why is Alberta ditching diversity, equity and inclusion in hiring practices?
candidates.description: Are hiring policies that strive for workplace diversity actually a problem that needs solving? Or is the UCP government engaging in political posturing? Panelists who spoke to CBC's West of Centre are split on the answer.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: COVID-19 school disruptions still impacting students today, learning loss report finds
candidates.description: A new report says Canadian students are still feeling the impact of the COVID pandemic's massive upset to their schooling, with declining achievement — particularly in math — and a discrepancy between standardized test scores and the grades kids receive in class.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: People called this Elora, Ont., company for a washer it supposedly sells. Except it doesn't even make washers
candidates.description: This week, hundreds of people were making calls and sending emails and messages to an Elora, Ont., appliance maker wanting to buy their so-called revolutionary washing machine, the "Keel." The problem? Elora's Stirling Marathon doesn't even make washers. The company is a victim of a scam Youtube video generated with artificial intelligence that has since been taken down.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ford government spent nearly $46M on 2 ad campaigns, FOI docs reveal
candidates.description: The Ford government spent nearly $46 million on two ad campaigns that ran across various social media and video platforms over the course of the 2025-26 year, records obtained by the CBC through a freedom-of-information request show.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada appoints new Indigenous languages commissioner
candidates.description: Dorothy Myo has been appointed Canada's new commissioner of Indigenous languages, a role mandated to support the revitalization of Indigenous languages across Canada.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: With increase of funding, Canada's sports leaders know there is expectation to increase participation
candidates.description: The distribution of increased funding in Canadian has begun and with an emphasis on participation, national sport organizations will have to get to work on new ideas and ways to bring more people into their sports.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada's Dabrowski, Brazil's Stefani advance to semifinals at WTA Finals after perfect group stage
candidates.description: Ottawa’s Gabriela Dabrowski and Brazil’s Luisa Stefani advanced to the doubles semifinals at the WTA Finals after defeating Latvia’s Jelena Ostapenko and Taiwan’s Su-Wei Hsieh 2-6, 7-6 (2), 10-3 on Friday in Indian Wells, Calif.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Alberta government asks judge to dismiss First Nation’s challenge of its sovereignty act
candidates.description: Alberta's government is asking a judge to strike down a First Nation's constitutional challenge of its sovereignty act, arguing the law hasn't had any impact on treaty rights.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: New Orleans port sues for control of China-linked tanker that crashed into cruise ship
candidates.description: Just hours after a tanker in New Orleans lost its steering and slammed into a docked river cruise boat, the city's port sued to make sure federal investigators can seize the vessel that is owned by a subsidiary of a Chinese company.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: European security plan floated by U.S. would benefit Putin, Zelenskyy says
candidates.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the United States had raised the possibility of a new security framework for Europe as part of efforts to end Russia’s war in Ukraine, warning that Moscow could use such discussions to weaken NATO and reshape the continent’s borders.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Carney says he will not boycott APEC 'family photo' with Putin
candidates.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney says he will participate in an upcoming group photo with Russian President Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit out of respect for the host, Chinese President Xi Jinping.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canadian judge decries U.S. sanctions of International Criminal Court as 'attack in favour of impunity'
candidates.description: Kimberly Prost, a Canadian judge at the International Criminal Court, was sanctioned by the Trump administration last August. Despite impacts including cancelled credit cards and frozen bank accounts, she says attempts to intimidate her and other court officials are 'futile.'
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Miracle on the Mississippi': All aboard river cruise boat survive crash with tanker in New Orleans
candidates.description: A tanker in New Orleans that apparently lost its steering slammed into a docked river cruise boat with 180 people aboard Friday, the mayor said. All aboard survived after the crash prompted a massive rescue operation for passengers and crew who plunged into the Mississippi River as the ship took on water and began to topple over.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Microsoft services fully restored after global outage
candidates.description: Microsoft said on Saturday that services had fully recovered across Teams, Outlook and its other products, ending a global outage that crippled online communications ‌for businesses and governments for over 24 hours.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: UN hails progress in Ebola response, cites insecurity as biggest challenge
candidates.description: UN health officials on Friday hailed progress in the Ebola response six months after the ​outbreak first prompted global concerns, but cautioned that ‌the disease continues to spread to more remote and dangerous parts of Congo.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Spanish goalkeeper barred 12 games for collision leading to death of Tenerife striker
candidates.description: While Spain mourns the death of a soccer player who suffered a cardiac arrest after an on-field collision, the emergency medical treatment he received is falling under scrutiny.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What the Jensen Huang scandal means for Trump and his administration
candidates.description: Jensen Huang's 33-year tenure as the CEO of chip-making giant Nvidia is now finished, but the political repercussions of his affair with an alleged Chinese spy are only just beginning.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: U.S. Treasury Secretary frustrated by Commerce Department's inaction on Nvidia chips
candidates.description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Friday he was frustrated with the Commerce Department's delay in placing restrictions on Nvidia chip exports to a company led by an alleged Chinese spy.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Russell Brand accused by 6 women of sexual misconduct, assault following rape conviction
candidates.description: Six more women have come forward alleging sexual misconduct and predatory behaviour by ex-comedian Russell Brand, according to an investigation by the U.K.-based The Times, following his conviction on rape and sexual assault earlier this week.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: U.K. police launch sex offence investigation into children’s author and comedian David Walliams
candidates.description: London police said on Friday they are investigating children’s author and TV personality David Walliams for serious sexual offences, after news outlets reported that he used his fame to groom girls and young women for sex. The Metropolitan Police said it had received a number of allegations of past abuse following a joint investigation by ITV News and the Guardian newspaper.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: NHL indicates Finland's block on Russian athletes could affect future games there
candidates.description: The NHL will consider Finland's plans to prevent Russian athletes entering the country when deciding whether to stage more regular-season games there in future, the league told The Associated Press.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: UN nuclear watchdog increasingly concerned about Iranian enrichment plant, report says
candidates.description: The United Nations nuclear watchdog is "increasingly concerned" about a uranium-enrichment plant at Isfahan that Iran declared to it last year but has still not let the watchdog inspect, it said in a confidential report on Friday seen by Reuters and The Associated Press.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Russian federation head Tretiak says it will seek compensation if barred from world juniors in Alberta
candidates.description: Russian hockey federation president Vladislav Tretiak is threatening to seek compensation from Canada and push for the relocation or cancellation of next month's world junior championship in Alberta if Russia is barred from competing.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Minimum wage hasn't kept pace with the cost of living across Canada, new reports show
candidates.description: Of the 59 cities and regions in reports for every province reviewed by CBC News, none had a provincial minimum wage equal to the calculated living wage — the amount a full-time worker needs to meet their basic needs, manage unexpected expenses and participate meaningfully in their community.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Alberta announces royalty program as part of plan to double oilsands production
candidates.description: The province says the OGP is designed to lower upfront financial barriers to new projects and expansions, particularly as proponents of the Pacific Link pipeline look for companies to fill upcoming capacity.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: The Nvidia scandal has wiped away $1T in value. What that means for your investments
candidates.description: Nvidia shares plunged early Thursday after CEO Jensen Huang resigned, before climbing back up to finish the day down 4.3 per cent. It's bad news for industry-watchers, but touches regular investors too because of the chipmaker's weight in major stock indexes.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Feds say Stellantis owes 'hundreds of millions' in subsidies, company offers $24M
candidates.description: Automaker Stellantis says it will pay back $24 million in federal subsidies after it announced plans to sell its Brampton, Ont. assembly plant — but Industry Minister Mélanie Joly says the company owes far more than what it is offering.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Microsoft outage continues as planned fixes are not working as expected, company says
candidates.description: A widespread Microsoft outage that began Thursday afternoon continues to affect many of the tech giant's apps and tools, including email, Teams and Copilot.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Copper wire upgrade caused nationwide flight suspension, US transport secretary says
candidates.description: The US government is trying to find out whether the chaos was caused by "incompetence" or faulty equipment.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: US has floated Ukraine ceding Donbas for Nato membership, Zelensky says
candidates.description: The US has not confirmed the Ukrainian president's comments which follow meetings US envoys had with him and Russia's Vladimir Putin.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Italy fines Meta €805m over accessing users' photos
candidates.description: The social media giant is accused of not informing 20 million users it had access to their photos.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Second catch attempt for SpaceX Starship rocket
candidates.description: The attempt follows an unsuccessful effort to catch of the rocket’s booster which instead came down in the ocean.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Sotheby's auction of $180m Van Gogh challenged over claims it was 'sold under duress'
candidates.description: Sotheby's says it will work with the heirs of a family who had previously owned the artwork to try and reach a solution.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Nigeria cautions against travel via Ethiopia's main airport due to altitude
candidates.description: The foreign ministry in Abuja says 6 Nigerians with underlying health problems have died this year while transiting through Addis Ababa.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'We'll get home one day' - US travellers impacted by nationwide ground stop
candidates.description: Passengers throughout the country were impacted over what the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) describes as “safety and communication issues”.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: Cruise ship overturns after collision with tanker in New Orleans
candidates.description: Around 130 people were rescued from a cruise ship after it was struck by a tanker while docked in New Orleans, Louisiana on Friday.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: Divers explore US ship sunk off Florida coast to create new reef
candidates.description: The ship was intentionally sunk off the coast of Florida in order to create the world's largest artificial ocean reef.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Will the Eurovision Song Contest succeed in Asia?
candidates.description: The world’s biggest and longest-running song contest is coming to Asia, with eleven countries competing in Bangkok, Thailand on Saturday.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Military cemetery decorum: The tradition behind Hegseth's Veterans Day reprimand
candidates.description: BBC's Bernd Debusmann breaks down why Defence Secretary Hegseth's group was reprimanded at Arlington National Cemetery and the history behind its strict rules of conduct.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?
candidates.description: Jojo was poached as an infant and grew up in captivity. His keepers want to find him a friend - but it's not straightforward.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: How the Jensen Huang scandal created a headache for business-friendly Singapore
candidates.description: The scandal has cast a spotlight on Singapore's success as a chip hub - and a location for alleged illicit trade.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Rosenberg: Uncompromising Putin ups demands for peace with Ukraine
candidates.description: The fact the question of European security now features in discussions is viewed in Moscow as a victory, BBC Russia Editor Steve Rosenberg says.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Pressure grows on Trump's Commerce Secretary Lutnick in fallout from Nvidia scandal
candidates.description: Scott Bessent told CNBC that several government agencies "were in favour of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Courts, spies and MPs: How the Microsoft outage has been felt around the world
candidates.description: From city governments in the US to spy agencies in Australia, the Microsoft outage is being felt around the world.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House
candidates.description: Jensen Huang's personal life may have triggered the crisis, but the questions now reach into the White House itself.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: What happened overnight with the Microsoft global outage?
candidates.description: Microsoft is struggling to fix a global outage, with services including Teams, Outlook and AI software Copilot affected by "connectivity problems".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Bluetongue virus confirmed on County Down farm
candidates.description: Officials from the Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs said the virus had been detected in three sheep.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: What could El Niño mean for winter weather in the US and Canada?
candidates.description: El Niño winters typically bring more rain in the southern USA and drier, warmer conditions further north but the impacts on snowfall are complex.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: How many sewage spills have happened in your part of Scotland?
candidates.description: More than 76,000 sewage spills were recorded at overflow sites previously unmonitored by Scottish Water, BBC Scotland News analysis has found.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Flood victim, 95, lived in Wetherspoons until she died after her home was destroyed
candidates.description: Jean Powell kept asking when she could go back to her flat, which was flooded when the River Monnow burst its banks.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Fuel crisis and protests pressure Chile's far-right president
candidates.description: Chile's far-right President José Antonio Kast is facing mounting public anger, as rising fuel prices trigger transport strikes and protests across the country.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: What's Trump's strategy now with Iran? To keep things as they are
candidates.description: President Trump says the "status quo" is what Gulf Arab allies want as the Iran war hits a stalemate and the U.S. midterms force a pivot from threats of attacks to economic pressure.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Nvidia CEO steps down. And, Sen. Chris Van Hollen to run for majority leader
candidates.description: Nvidia's chief financial officer has been appointed interim CEO after Jensen Huang stepped down from the role. And, Sen. Chris Van Hollen says he will challenge Chuck Schumer for majority leader.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Nvidia's interim CEO inherits risky AI bets and a legal mess
candidates.description: AI expert Gary Marcus breaks down what's at stake for Nvidia and the mess its new CEO has inherited.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: These economists say in-person work boosts creativity, but office mandates fall short
candidates.description: A pair economists argue in a new book that people are more creative and productive when they work together in person. But it's not enough for employers to simply order workers back to the office.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Is there an opening for Nvidia's competitors, now that Jensen Huang is out?
candidates.description: NPR's Scott Detrow talks with Dylan Patel of the AI and semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis about Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia, and whether it opens up the field for Nvidia's competitors.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Does Europe regret its bet on U.S. defense?
candidates.description: Europe bet big on American defense technology and they're now paying the price. Years-long backlogs are underway due to production delays and the U.S. own military needs.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: SpaceX's giant rocket may leave NASA in the dust
candidates.description: As it races to develop its new massive rocket, the space launch company is preparing to retire NASA's main ride to the International Space Station.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: CEO Jensen Huang resigns from chip giant Nvidia
candidates.description: The chip giant Nvidia announced that CEO Jensen Huang was stepping down following allegations that he'd had extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A new policy could help solve the U.S. organ shortage. Critics say it's unethical
candidates.description: New guidelines are supposed to protect organ donors in a retrieval procedure that keeps blood flowing through livers, kidneys, lungs and hearts. But bioethicists have troubling questions.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: How Sen. Chris Van Hollen plans to flex Democratic power on the foreign aid front
candidates.description: He's the ranking member of the Senate Foreign Relations Subcommittee that oversees health aid and he's just announced he's running for Majority Leader. He spoke to NPR about his foreign aid vision.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Happy World Kindness Day! Check out our kind photos of kindness to humans -- and cats
candidates.description: Friday, November 13 is World Kindness Day. Your mission: Do something kind. Small acts of kindness definitely count!
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Kratom and 7-OH can feel like 'a miracle.' They can also be addictive
candidates.description: In the last decade, strong support for kratom and 7-OH products have kept them federally legal. That's started to change. A crackdown for some highly potent products related to kratom is coming.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Fed up with the healthcare industry, this red state capped insulin prices for patients
candidates.description: Republicans and Democrats in North Dakota worked together to limit what people with diabetes have to pay for insulin, joining a growing bipartisan push across the country to protect patients.
candidates.author: NPR
